insight.title: Why You Catch Up Faster by Slowing Down
insight.subtitle: How reducing your speed helps you reach your goals sooner.

sections.text: To catch an object in orbit, you don’t aim at it and accelerate. You slow down. This drop in velocity lowers your altitude, which actually increases your speed relative to the earth below.

We treat deadlines like targets we must chase with force. But high-pressure acceleration clouds judgment. By lowering your intensity, you drop into a "lower orbit" where you can finally see the path clearly.
This is about efficiency, not laziness. When you stop rushing, you stop creating the mistakes that usually slow you down. You reach the destination sooner simply by refusing to chase it recklessly.
Try this today: When you feel rushed to finish a task today, pause for ten seconds to check your direction.
True speed is the absence of unnecessary friction.

news.title: Report: Losing your job to AI doesn’t just lead to unemployment, it leaves lasting scars
news.description: AI-driven job losses may not just make it harder for affected workers to find employment in the short term but also could leave a yearslong “scarring,” marked by depressed income, delayed homeownership and even the lower probability of marriage, according to a new research report from Goldman Sachs.
news.why: Automation could permanently shrink your paycheck and make new hiring difficult.

news.why: Domestic power helps keep your monthly home electricity bills stable and cheap.

news.title: Photos: NASA releases first images from moon flyby
news.description: During the mission's loop around the moon, the crew took geological observations of places of interest on the lunar surface using their own eyes and snapping thousands of photos of the surface.
news.why: Space exploration helps improve the GPS and communication services you use.
